figures.caption: Figure S1. Reconstructed X-ray CT image slice of the pristine cell for Case A. Large LPSC particles are evident throughout the SSE, with various pores in the LPSC apparent prior to deposition. Video S1 includes the region outlined in purple, magnified on the right. Image segmentation was conducted in a smaller subvolume (outlined in blue in the image on the right) to track crack evolution during lithium deposition and stripping (Figs. 2-3a, b). The extended subvolume (outlined in green) was segmented to track the total volume throughout the entire SSE pellet thickness in Fig. 3c.

figures.label: S4
figures.caption: Figure S4. Histogram of the measured grayscale pixel intensities for original pores and new cracks caused during lithium deposition (presumably lithium-filled cracks). Pixel counts are defined as the number of pixels along the line scan with an intensity corresponding to voids or lithium. Line scans were taken across 28 scans and plotted. The grayscale intensity distribution for pores/voids and lithium overlap, thus indicating that intensity tracking is not sufficient to differentiate the two.
